headline: 12,000 Bangladeshis can go to Italy via legal channels annually
summary: State Minister for Local Government Mir Shah Alam announced the opportunity for citizens to migrate with their families to Italy legally.
details: State Minister for Local Government Mir Shah Alam announced that 12,000 Bangladeshis, including their families, have the opportunity to migrate to Italy through legal channels every year.
The announcement followed a meeting with the Italian Ambassador to Bangladesh, Antonio Alessandro, at the Secretariat on Monday.
During the meeting, the Italian Ambassador expressed concern over the number of Bangladeshi citizens attempting to migrate to Italy through illegal routes.
Ambassador Alessandro urged the government to raise awareness and discourage citizens from attempting illegal migration to avoid risks.
Minister Mir Shah Alam also requested Italy's cooperation in providing third-language education and vocational training for those interested in moving to the country.
caption:
12,000 legal spots available annually for Bangladeshis to move to Italy with their families.

State Minister for Local Government Mir Shah Alam announced that 12,000 Bangladeshis, including their families, have the opportunity to migrate to Italy through legal channels every year.

The announcement followed a meeting with the Italian Ambassador to Bangladesh, Antonio Alessandro, at the Secretariat on Monday.

During the meeting, the Italian Ambassador expressed concern over the number of Bangladeshi citizens attempting to migrate to Italy through illegal routes.

Ambassador Alessandro urged the government to raise awareness and discourage citizens from attempting illegal migration to avoid risks.

Minister Mir Shah Alam also requested Italy's cooperation in providing third-language education and vocational training for those interested in moving to the country.

Source: Jamuna TV

headline: 75,000 depositors seek Tk 3,925 crore from Sammilito Islami Bank
summary: The newly merged bank begins disbursing funds to customers after receiving Tk 5,000 crore in liquidity support from Bangladesh Bank.
details: Around 75,000 customers have applied to withdraw their deposits from Sammilito Islami Bank in the first four days of this month, seeking a total of Tk 3,925 crore.
Sammilito Islami Bank was formed last year by merging five troubled Islamic banks: First Security Islami Bank, Global Islami Bank, Social Islami Bank, Union Bank, and EXIM Bank.
To facilitate these payments, Bangladesh Bank provided Tk 5,000 crore in liquidity support to the newly formed entity to help it meet withdrawal demands and restore normal operations.
The central bank has announced a scheme to repay the entire amount to depositors in phases, ensuring there will be no 'haircut' on the deposits.
Individual depositors are allowed to withdraw the principal amount of their deposits according to their needs starting from September 1.
Bank officials stated that they are verifying applications submitted at branches and sub-branches before handing over the money to depositors.
caption:
75,000 people are seeking nearly Tk 4,000 crore from one bank. Here is how the repayment process is underway.

Around 75,000 customers have applied to withdraw their deposits from Sammilito Islami Bank in the first four days of this month, seeking a total of Tk 3,925 crore.

Sammilito Islami Bank was formed last year by merging five troubled Islamic banks: First Security Islami Bank, Global Islami Bank, Social Islami Bank, Union Bank, and EXIM Bank.

To facilitate these payments, Bangladesh Bank provided Tk 5,000 crore in liquidity support to the newly formed entity to help it meet withdrawal demands and restore normal operations.

The central bank has announced a scheme to repay the entire amount to depositors in phases, ensuring there will be no 'haircut' on the deposits.

Individual depositors are allowed to withdraw the principal amount of their deposits according to their needs starting from September 1.

Bank officials stated that they are verifying applications submitted at branches and sub-branches before handing over the money to depositors.
